baseline.method: one OLS model per horizon on same-horizon controls whose labels were available before each UTC day (and before a checkpoint's cutoff); residual difference

checkpoints.rule: a checkpoint is computed once, from data known by its cutoff, and never recomputed

comparison.rationale: price hypothesised to move toward sampled liquidation clusters (magnet); oriented toward the cluster

decision_timing.basis: as-of replay by a 6-hourly lab; decisions were not executed live

definitions.t_available: ASSUMED decision time = t_inputs + 60 s processing (not measured)
definitions.t_inputs: required-input availability (latest observed_at of the inputs)
definitions.t_persisted: actual time a lab run first computed and froze the decision

condition: When sampled long liquidation exposure within 2% of mark is large, does BTC fall more than at scheduled times?

costs.funding: Binance BTCUSDT settled 8h rates in (entry, exit]; longs pay positive
costs.status: assumption; verify fees before relying on net figures

inputs._note: cutoff 2026-10-06T00:55Z; records with observed_at after the cutoff are ignored

exclusions: sampled accounts only; never market inventory
failures: prospective: 1047 sampled snapshots; the design needs 1344

horizons.rule: Only the primary horizon, fixed in the design before any data, decides checkpoints, status and skill proposals; secondary horizons are descriptive and cannot override a failed primary or trigger a proposal on their own.

limitations: Decisions are as-of replays computed by a 6-hourly lab; decision times assume 60 s of processing after the last required input and were not executed live (t_persisted shows when each was actually computed).
Retained observations do not overlap in their label intervals; that does not make them independent. Intervals resample dependence blocks (overlap or same UTC day).
Intervals are descriptive bootstrap intervals; the adjusted interval divides alpha by variants x looks (Bonferroni), which is conservative but not a formal test of profitability.
Net returns use cost model costs-1, whose fee and slippage values are assumptions (see VALIDATION.md).
'supported' means the declared criteria held on prospective replays; it is not proof of profitability.
